title: Negative: neural-field comets do not divide by themselves; at theta=0.5 a lone comet stays one 32-42 px bump (4/4 seeds), and below theta~0.495 it grows into a wave segment that wraps the domain or fragments, so the population's splits come from bars, not from comet fission
summary: In c20's neural-field world (sighting 20261025T1707-c20-neural-field-comets), labkit counts 12-13 persistent splits per run in the population. To ask whether a comet reproduces autonomously, the world was run to t=200 at theta 0.48-0.5 (seeds 0-3), every body except the median-size one was erased (u and a reset to 0) and the lone body followed for 600 time units with periodic labelling (isolate.py). At theta=0.5 (the sighting's value) the lone comet stays a single bump of 32-42 px and travels for the whole run on 4/4 seeds. At 0.49-0.495 it grows into a travelling wave segment that stays one body (often wrapping the periodic domain, up to ~1000 px) or sheds 1-2 pieces; at 0.485 segments grow and fragment into 8-17 bodies of very mixed size (31-880 px) on 3/4 seeds; at 0.48 one or two domain-wrapping bands form. So there is no regime with binary fission of a compact comet into two comets: below the stability edge growth is unbounded, and the splits in the population run are break-ups of bars made by collisions.

finding.operator: Amari neural field with linear adaptation and a difference-of-Gaussians kernel
finding.control: single-body isolation at five excitabilities (theta 0.48, 0.485, 0.49, 0.495, 0.5), 4 seeds each, T=600, periodic labelling

limits: One kernel shape and adaptation rate (g=2.5, eps=0.03); theta was the only parameter varied. A slow resource or a second inhibitory population might bound segment growth and turn break-up into fission; not tried. Isolation erases the neighbours' adaptation wakes, which may matter for bar formation.
